questions.title: Asking Questions
questions.explanation: Dari question words stay right where the answer would go, rather than moving to the front the way English does. "شما کجا هستید؟" is literally "You where are?" -- کجا (kojā, where) simply sits in the spot the place-answer would fill. The same is true for چی (chi, what), کی (kay, when), چرا (cherā, why), and چند (chand, how many).
questions.fact: چند (chand) does double duty: alone before a noun it means "how many/how much" (چند کتاب؟ "how many books?"), but with -م attached it becomes چندم ("which number in order") for asking someone's rank or position.

dialogue.native: من در یک دوکان کار می‌کنم.
چند سال است که آنجا کار می‌کنید؟
dialogue.en: How many years have you worked there?

prepositions-location.title: Saying Where Something Is
prepositions-location.explanation: Location words like در (in), نزدیک (near), دور (far from), زیر (under), and روی (on) come directly before the place they describe, just like English "in," "near," "under." کتاب روی میز است is "the book is on the table."
prepositions-location.fact: روی literally means "face" as a noun (as in چهره/روی, "face") -- "on top of" grew out of the image of something resting face-up on a surface.

dialogue.native: خانه شما نزدیک است یا دور؟
dialogue.en: Is your house near or far?

items.en: My father is a doctor.
My mother is a teacher.
My brother is an engineer.
He/She works at the market.
The cook works in the kitchen.
The farmer works in the field.
What work do you do?

items.dari: من با موتر به مکتب می‌روم.
items.en: I go to school by car.
items.translit: Man ba motar ba maktab miraum.

items.dari: او با بس به کار می‌رود.
items.en: He/She goes to work by bus.
items.translit: U ba bas ba kār miraud.

items.en: This road is big.
The airplane is in the sky.
The train goes very fast.
The boat is on the water.
Where is your car?
What is this?
Where are you?
When is he/she coming?
Why are you happy?
How many books do you have?
Which house is yours?
How do you go to the market?
The book is on the table.
The cat is under the chair.
Our house is near the market.
The school is far from home.
I am in the room.
He/She is in front of the door.
The money is in my hand.

items.dari: این خانه بزرگ است و آن خانه کوچک است.
items.en: This house is big and that house is small.
items.translit: In khāna bozorg ast wa ān khāna kuchak ast.

items.dari: موتر او دراز و بلند است.
items.en: His/her car is long and tall.
items.translit: Motar-e u derāz wa boland ast.

items.dari: کفش کوچک برای طفل خوب است.
items.en: Small shoes are good for a child.
items.translit: Kafsh-e kuchak barāy-e tefl khub ast.

items.dari: این کتاب کهنه است، آن کتاب نو است.
items.en: This book is old, that book is new.
items.translit: In kitāb kohna ast, ān kitāb naw ast.

items.en: A big house is expensive.
This table is narrow.
I am happy today.
He/She is sad.
We are tired.
Why are you angry?
He/She is afraid of the big dog.
I am calm.

items.dari: بعد از کار، من خسته می‌شوم.
items.en: After work, I get tired.
items.translit: Ba'd az kār, man khasta misham.

items.en: I have a pen and a notebook.
The teacher is in the classroom.
The students read the lesson.
We have an exam today.
He/She studies at university.
I am learning the Dari language.
This lesson is difficult.
What time is it now?
It is seven in the morning.

items.dari: من ساعت هشت به مکتب می‌روم.
items.en: I go to school at eight o'clock.
items.translit: Man sā'at hasht ba maktab miraum.

items.en: What time do you sleep at night?
We eat food at noon.
Yesterday, today, tomorrow.
He/She always comes on time.
My grandfather is very kind.

items.dari: مادربزرگ من در خانه ما است.
items.en: My grandmother is at our house.
items.translit: Mādarbozorg-e man dar khāna-ye mā ast.

items.en: My paternal uncle is a doctor.

items.dari: ماما و خاله من در کابل هستند.
items.en: My maternal uncle and aunt are in Kabul.
items.translit: Māmā wa khāla-ye man dar Kābul hastand.

items.en: My paternal aunt is a teacher.

items.dari: این طفل کوچک، نواسه من است.
items.en: This small child is my grandchild.
items.translit: In tefl-e kuchak, nawāsa-ye man ast.

items.en: I wake up early in the morning.
After that, I eat breakfast.

items.dari: من به مکتب می‌روم و درس می‌خوانم.
items.en: I go to school and study lessons.
items.translit: Man ba maktab miraum wa dars mikhwānam.

items.dari: ظهر با دوستان خود غذا می‌خورم.
items.en: At noon I eat with my friends.
items.translit: Zohr bā dostān-e khod ghazā mikhoram.

items.en: In the evening I come home.
At night I read a book and sleep.
How much is this?
What is the price of this book?
I want to buy apples.
The seller is in the shop.
My money is little.
This market is very big.

items.dari: او هر روز از بازار خرید می‌کند.
items.en: He/She shops at the market every day.
items.translit: U har roz az bāzār kharid mikonad.

items.en: I like tea.

items.dari: او رنگ آبی را دوست دارد.
items.en: He/She likes the color blue.
items.translit: U rang-e ābi rā dost dārad.

items.en: We like this book.
I have interest in music.

items.dari: شما کدام غذا را دوست دارید؟
items.en: Which food do you like?
items.translit: Shomā kudām ghazā rā dost dārid?

items.dari: او هوای سرد را دوست ندارد.
items.en: He/She does not like cold weather.
items.translit: U hawā-ye sard rā dost nadārad.

items.en: I always eat breakfast.
He/She usually goes to school.
We sometimes go to the market.
He/She never drinks tea.
I always read books.

items.dari: شما چند وقت به بازار می‌روید؟
items.en: How often do you go to the market?
items.translit: Shomā chand waqt ba bāzār miraid?

items.en: Hello, how are you?

items.dari: من خوب هستم، شما چطور هستید؟
items.en: I am good, how are you?
items.translit: Man khub hastam, shomā chetor hastid?

items.en: Are you working today or not?
Yes, I am working today.
What are you doing tomorrow?
Tomorrow I am going to the market.

items.dari: نام من احمد است و من از کابل هستم.
items.en: My name is Ahmad and I am from Kabul.
items.translit: Nām-e man Ahmad ast wa man az Kābul hastam.

items.dari: من هر روز به مکتب می‌روم و درس می‌خوانم.
items.en: I go to school and study every day.
items.translit: Man har roz ba maktab miraum wa dars mikhwānam.

items.dari: خانه ما بزرگ است و نزدیک بازار است.
items.en: Our house is big and near the market.
items.translit: Khāna-ye mā bozorg ast wa nazdik-e bāzār ast.

items.dari: من چای و نان را دوست دارم.
items.en: I like tea and bread.
items.translit: Man chāy wa nān rā dost dāram.

items.dari: برادر من داکتر است و در شفاخانه کار می‌کند.
items.en: My brother is a doctor and works at the hospital.
items.translit: Barādar-e man dāktar ast wa dar shafākhāna kār mikonad.

items.dari: نام شما چیست؟ -- نام من مریم است.
items.en: What is your name? -- My name is Maryam.
items.translit: Nām-e shomā chist? -- Nām-e man Maryam ast.

items.dari: شما از کجا هستید؟ -- من از هرات هستم.
items.en: Where are you from? -- I am from Herat.
items.translit: Shomā az kojā hastid? -- Man az Herāt hastam.

items.dari: چند سال دارید؟ -- من بیست سال دارم.
items.en: How old are you? -- I am twenty years old.
items.translit: Chand sāl dārid? -- Man bist sāl dāram.

items.dari: چه کار می‌کنید؟ -- من معلم هستم.
items.en: What work do you do? -- I am a teacher.
items.translit: Che kār mikonid? -- Man mo'alim hastam.

items.dari: کدام رنگ را دوست دارید؟ -- من رنگ سبز را دوست دارم.
items.en: Which color do you like? -- I like the color green.
items.translit: Kudām rang rā dost dārid? -- Man rang-e sabz rā dost dāram.
